Bayesian Gaussian mixture model with explicit cluster assignments, sampled
with a Gibbs combination of particle Gibbs (for the discrete assignments)
and HMC (for means and weights). The data have three clusters and the
model is over-specified with `K = 4` components.

Source: `EnvBRAN/test_gmm.ipynb` (titled "Infinite GMM"; the `.html`
render and `.md` export were dropped).

::: {.callout-note}
The original used the Turing ≤ 0.35 syntax `Gibbs(PG(100, :k), HMC(0.05, 10, :μ, :w))`;
current Turing pairs variables with samplers: `Gibbs(:k => PG(100), (:μ, :w) => HMC(0.05, 10))`.
:::

```{julia}
using ExposomicsJulia
using DataFrames, Statistics, LinearAlgebra, Plots, StatsBase
using Distributions
using Turing
```

```{julia}
w = [0.33, 0.33, 0.34]
μ = [[5.0, 5.0], [10.0, 0.0], [0.0, 10.0]]
mixturemodel = MixtureModel([MvNormal(μₖ, 0.1 * I) for μₖ in μ], w)

N = 80
xa = rand(mixturemodel, N);
scatter(xa[1, :], xa[2, :]; label = "")
```

```{julia}
@model function gaussian_mixture_model4(x)
    K = 4
    # cluster means
    μ ~ filldist(MvNormal(zeros(2), 2.0 * I), K)
    # cluster weights (Dirichlet with αₖ = 2)
    w ~ Dirichlet(K, 2.0)
    distribution_assignments = Categorical(w)

    D, N = size(x)
    distribution_clusters = [MvNormal(m, 2.0 * I) for m in eachcol(μ)]

    # assignment and likelihood for each datum
    k = Vector{Int}(undef, N)
    for i in 1:N
        k[i] ~ distribution_assignments
        x[:, i] ~ distribution_clusters[k[i]]
    end
    return k
end

model = gaussian_mixture_model4(xa);
```

```{julia}
#| eval: false
sampler = Gibbs(:k => PG(100), (:μ, :w) => HMC(0.05, 10))
@time chains = sample(model, sampler, 100);
# multiple chains: sample(model, sampler, MCMCThreads(), 100, 3)
```

Posterior median cluster assignment of each point:

```{julia}
#| eval: false
mdn = vec(median(draws(chains, :k); dims = 1))
countmap(mdn)
```
